error_summary: SqlBulkCopy failed with SqlException login failed — Managed Identity not added as SQL user after infrastructure redeployment
root_cause: Terraform recreated the Azure SQL server (name change in terraform.tfvars triggered destroy+create). The managed identity id-positionprocessor was added as a SQL user manually after the original deployment but was not in Terraform state. After the server was recreated, the manual SQL user was lost. InsertPositionsActivity failed on conn.OpenAsync() with SqlException: Login failed for user id-positionprocessor. The error appeared immediately on the first run after the redeployment at 06:00 UTC.
resolution: 1. Confirmed identity existed in Azure AD but not in SQL: SELECT name FROM sys.database_principals WHERE name = 'id-positionprocessor' returned no rows. 2. Connected to FinanceDb via break-glass SQL admin account from Azure Portal Query Editor. 3. Ran: CREATE USER [id-positionprocessor] FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER; ALTER ROLE db_datawriter ADD MEMBER [id-positionprocessor]; ALTER ROLE db_datareader ADD MEMBER [id-positionprocessor]; 4. Manually triggered rerun via POST /api/trigger?date=2026-05-21. Run completed successfully.
prevention: 1. Add SQL user creation to Terraform using null_resource with sqlcmd provisioner so it runs automatically after server creation. 2. Add post-deployment smoke test: attempt SQL connection from Function App and alert if login fails. 3. Document SQL user setup step in runbook — it is not in Terraform and must be done manually after any SQL server recreate.

error_summary: LoadTradesActivity failed with BlobErrorCode BlobNotFound — trade file not uploaded before scheduler triggered
root_cause: The upstream data feed that uploads trade CSV files to Blob Storage experienced a 2-hour delay due to a network issue at the data vendor. The Scheduler fired at 06:00 UTC as scheduled. LoadTradesActivity called blobClient.DownloadContentAsync() on trades/2026-04-15/positions.csv which did not exist yet. Azure SDK threw RequestFailedException with BlobErrorCode.BlobNotFound (HTTP 404). The orchestrator caught this as an unhandled exception and wrote FAILED to ProcessingRunLog. The file arrived at 08:12 UTC but no automatic retry existed.
resolution: 1. Identified missing blob via Azure Portal Storage Browser — file not present at 06:00, arrived at 08:12. 2. Manually triggered rerun: POST /api/trigger?date=2026-04-15 after confirming file was present. 3. Run completed successfully with 847 positions inserted.
prevention: 1. Add blob existence check in LoadTradesActivity before download: if (!await blobClient.ExistsAsync()) throw new FileNotFoundException with clear message. 2. Implement retry in orchestrator: if LoadTradesActivity returns FileNotFoundException, wait 30 minutes and retry up to 3 times using context.CreateTimer() before marking as FAILED. 3. Add upstream file arrival monitoring: alert if trades/YYYY-MM-DD/positions.csv not present by 05:45 UTC.

error_summary: SqlBulkCopy timeout — BulkInsertAsync took 142 seconds and hit SqlBulkCopy BulkCopyTimeout of 120 seconds during large trade file
root_cause: End of quarter trade volume was 3x normal (18,400 trades vs average 800). InsertPositionsActivity produced 2,340 position rows. SqlBulkCopy was configured with BulkCopyTimeout = 120 seconds. The bulk insert took 142 seconds due to SQL S1 tier (20 DTUs) being CPU-bound. The operation failed with SqlException: Timeout expired. The operation was started before 120 seconds had elapsed and the timeout has expired. ProcessingRunLog showed FAILED status. App Insights dependency trace showed the BulkInsertAsync dependency duration as 120,000ms marked as failed.
resolution: 1. Identified via App Insights: dependency trace showed BulkInsertAsync duration exactly 120s (timeout). 2. Scaled SQL from S1 to S3 (100 DTUs) via Azure Portal — immediate, no restart. 3. Increased BulkCopyTimeout from 120 to 300 in InsertPositionsActivity code and redeployed. 4. Manually retriggered. Run completed in 38 seconds with S3.
prevention: 1. Increase BulkCopyTimeout to 300 seconds in InsertPositionsActivity permanently. 2. Add DTU monitoring alert: alert when DTU consumption > 80% for > 5 minutes. 3. Scale SQL to S3 for end-of-month and end-of-quarter runs as a scheduled action. 4. Consider upgrading to General Purpose vCore tier for auto-scaling capability.

error_summary: LoadTradesActivity failed with RequestFailedException — Blob Storage private endpoint DNS resolution returned NXDOMAIN after VNet DNS change
root_cause: A network configuration change added a new custom DNS resolver to the VNet. The DNS Private Resolver was not configured with a conditional forwarding rule for privatelink.blob.core.windows.net. DNS queries for stfinancepoc01.blob.core.windows.net returned NXDOMAIN instead of the private endpoint IP. BlobServiceClient threw RequestFailedException: No such host is known. The Function App has vnet_route_all_enabled = true so all DNS queries go through the VNet DNS. The change was applied at 02:00 UTC maintenance window and the 06:00 run was the first affected.
resolution: 1. Confirmed DNS issue: ran nslookup stfinancepoc01.blob.core.windows.net from a VM inside the VNet — returned NXDOMAIN. Expected private endpoint IP from snet-pe subnet. 2. Added conditional forwarding rule to DNS Private Resolver for privatelink.blob.core.windows.net pointing to 168.63.129.16 (Azure DNS). 3. DNS resolved correctly within 60 seconds. 4. Retriggered run — completed successfully.
prevention: 1. Any VNet DNS change must be validated by running nslookup for all private endpoint FQDNs from inside the VNet before applying. Required FQDNs: stfinancepoc01.blob.core.windows.net and sql-finance-poc01.database.windows.net. 2. Add synthetic DNS monitor: periodic nslookup test from within VNet, alert on NXDOMAIN. 3. DNS changes require sign-off from platform team and must be tested in dev VNet first.

error_summary: InsertPositionsActivity failed with FormatException — CSV file contained a corrupted row with non-numeric Price field causing decimal.Parse to throw
root_cause: The upstream data feed for 2026-05-10 produced a CSV file where row T047 had the Price field populated with the string N/A instead of a decimal number. The ParseCsv method in LoadTradesActivity called decimal.Parse(cols[4].Trim()) without try/catch or TryParse. FormatException: Input string was not in a correct format was thrown. The exception propagated up through LoadTradesActivity, was caught by the orchestrator's top-level try/catch, and written to ProcessingRunLog as FAILED. The entire run failed even though only 1 of 420 rows was corrupted.
resolution: 1. Identified corrupted row by downloading the CSV from blob storage and inspecting manually. Row T047 had Price=N/A. 2. Fixed the CSV manually (replaced N/A with correct price 148.75 from reference data). Re-uploaded to blob storage. 3. Manually retriggered run. 4. Deployed code fix: replaced decimal.Parse with decimal.TryParse in ParseCsv — rows that fail parsing are skipped with a warning log instead of throwing.
prevention: 1. Replace decimal.Parse with decimal.TryParse in LoadTradesActivity.ParseCsv for all numeric fields (Quantity, Price). Log skipped rows as warnings. 2. Add post-parse validation: if skipped row count > 5% of total rows, fail with a clear DataQualityException rather than silently continuing. 3. Add upstream data validation at the feed provider to reject files with non-numeric price fields. 4. Add integration test with a malformed CSV to verify graceful handling.
